name: Victoria Bridge, Cambridge, England
facts: Victoria Bridge, completed in 1890, was engineered as a single-arch structure to span the River Cam, linking the then village of Chesterton with the growing city of Cambridge.
Frederic Wace, Cambridge's mayor, laid the foundation stone on 4 November 1889 and officially opened the bridge a year later, on 11 December 1890.
In 1992, the bridge underwent a strengthening rebuild to preserve its historic single-arch design while accommodating modern traffic demands.
